title: Queensland End-of-Lease Checklist: Get Your Full Bond Back
excerpt: Know exactly what tenants must fix, what landlords cover, and how to organise cleaning, repairs and rubbish removal before your Queensland lease ends.
body:
Moving out of a Queensland rental can feel overwhelming, especially when your bond — often several thousand dollars — is on the line. Getting it back in full comes down to understanding what the law requires, what your landlord is actually responsible for, and booking the right services in the right order.

## What Queensland Law Says About End-of-Lease Condition

Under the *Residential Tenancies and Rooming Accommodation Act 2008* (Queensland), tenants must return the property in the same condition as when they moved in, allowing for **fair wear and tear**. This is a meaningful distinction.

**Fair wear and tear** includes:
- Minor scuffs on walls from furniture
- Small nail holes from picture hooks
- Carpet pile compression in high-traffic areas
- Fading caused by sunlight

**Tenant responsibility** (not fair wear and tear):
- Stains, burns or deep scratches on floors or carpet
- Large holes or gouges in walls
- Mould caused by poor ventilation habits (e.g. no exhaust fan use)
- Broken windows, blinds or door handles caused by misuse
- Pet damage of any kind
- Uncleaned ovens, rangehoods, bathrooms or toilets

The Residential Tenancies Authority (RTA) provides a free dispute resolution service if you and your landlord disagree about condition, so document everything.

## What Landlords Must Fix

Landlords cannot use the bond to cover costs that are genuinely their responsibility. These include:

- Wear that is consistent with the property's age and the tenancy length
- Pre-existing damage that was noted on the original entry condition report
- Repainting walls after a long tenancy (typically five or more years) if the paint has simply aged
- Replacing appliances that have failed due to normal age and use
- General garden maintenance beyond what was specified in the lease

If an item was already damaged when you moved in and you documented it on the Entry Condition Report (Form 1a), the landlord cannot charge you for it at the end. Signed, dated photos stored in your email or cloud are your best protection.

## The Exit Condition Report Is Critical

At the end of your tenancy, complete the **Exit Condition Report (Form 14a)**, available free from the RTA website. Walk through every room, note condition, take timestamped photos and video, and return it to the property manager within three business days of vacating.

Do this even if your property manager says it isn't necessary. It creates a legal record.

## How to Book Services — and in What Order

Sequence matters. Booking the wrong service at the wrong time wastes money.

| Step | Service | Timing |
|------|---------|--------|
| 1 | Pest control (if required by lease) | 3–5 days before vacating |
| 2 | Rubbish and hard waste removal | 2–3 days before vacating |
| 3 | Carpet and upholstery cleaning | 1–2 days before vacating |
| 4 | Bond/end-of-lease clean | Final 1–2 days |
| 5 | Wall patching and paint touch-ups | Before the clean, not after |
| 6 | Key handover and exit report | On or before lease end date |

**Patch walls before cleaning**, not after — dusty filler ruins a freshly wiped surface. Book cleaners for the day after your rubbish is gone so they're not working around junk.

## Choosing the Right Cleaners

Not all cleaning services are equal for bond purposes. When comparing providers:

- Ask specifically for **end-of-lease or bond cleaning**, not a standard house clean — the scope is different
- Confirm the quote includes oven, rangehood filters, window tracks, skirting boards and light fittings
- Get a written quote and ask whether they offer a **re-clean guarantee** if the property manager finds something
- In Queensland's climate, mould treatment in bathrooms and laundries is often needed — confirm it's included

Many Queensland property managers will accept a professional cleaner's receipt as evidence that the property was cleaned to a reasonable standard, which can help in any RTA dispute.

## Rubbish Removal: Don't Leave It to Chance

Council hard waste collections are not reliable enough to plan around when you have a fixed vacate date. Book a private rubbish removal service two to three days before your cleaning appointment. Leave the property empty of all belongings before cleaners arrive — every item left behind costs you time and potentially bond money.

## Your Actionable Move-Out Timeline

Four weeks before your vacate date, pull out your original Entry Condition Report and compare it room by room with the current state of the property. Write a list of anything that needs attention. Then book services in the sequence above, working backwards from your handover date. Submit your Exit Condition Report promptly, retain copies, and lodge your bond refund claim with the RTA as soon as the keys are returned.

The RTA's online bond refund process typically takes two to three business days once both parties agree. If your landlord disputes the claim, the RTA's free conciliation service is the first step — not a tribunal, and not a solicitor.

Staying organised and methodical is the difference between getting your full bond back and spending weeks arguing over a dirty oven.
